one_liner: Low-level C++ utility library whose charconv module (xtoa/atox) beats std::to_chars and std::from_chars on integers.
what_it_does: c4core is a general-purpose low-level C++ utility library (string views, spans, allocators, formatting, error handling). Its charconv module converts 8/16/32/64-bit signed/unsigned integers and floats to/from decimal ASCII via c4::to_chars()/c4::from_chars() (aliased xtoa()/atox(), built on write_dec()/read_dec() etc.). The API takes a c4::substr/csubstr buffer and returns size_t (chars written) or bool (success) rather than std::to_chars_result/from_chars_result, so it is not a literal drop-in for std::to_chars/from_chars.
how_it_is_fast: For integers, c4core uses its own digit-counting and decimal-digit extraction routines (digits_dec()/write_dec()/read_dec()) with no locale handling, format-flag dispatch, or allocation, avoiding overhead present in libstdc++/MSVC STL's std::to_chars/from_chars. For float/double, c4core does not implement its own parsing algorithm: from_chars for floating types is answered by the bundled fast_float submodule (already catalogued separately) when C++17 and the fastfloat option are enabled (the default), so the float speedup is fast_float's algorithm, not original c4core code.
when_to_use: Hot loops converting many fixed-width integers (u8-u64, i8-i64) to/from decimal ASCII, e.g. log lines or serialization formatting
Already using c4core/rapidyaml or want one low-level utility library instead of many point solutions
Comfortable with a substr/csubstr buffer API instead of std::to_chars' pointer-pair + result-struct signature
Building on a toolchain without full C++17 <charconv>: c4core still gets integer speedups on C++11, and floats route through fast_float
Want MIT-licensed source that can be vendored as a single amalgamated header (tools/amalgamate.py)
when_not_to_use: Only need fast float/double parsing: use fast_float directly, since c4core's float path is just fast_float underneath with extra library weight on top
Want a minimal, single-purpose charconv library: c4core pulls in a large general-purpose utility library (span, allocators, error handling, etc.)
Need the exact std::to_chars/from_chars call signature for drop-in replacement without call-site changes
Need independently-verified numbers: only the project's own README/CI benchmarks exist (evidence tier C), with no hardware/CPU disclosed
Targeting old MSVC (<2019): std::to_chars/from_chars interop is unavailable, and the README's text table itself is from an older g++11.2 run vs. current CI's newer compilers

integration.form: source-drop (CMake subproject/static lib) or single-header via tools/amalgamate.py
integration.dependencies: fast_float (bundled git submodule, used for float/double parsing when C++17 + fastfloat option enabled, the default); sg14 inplace_function (BSL-1.0) and debugbreak (BSD-2-Clause) are bundled for other parts of c4core, not charconv itself
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 minimum for the library and integer xtoa/atox; C++17 with MSVC2019+/GCC or a compiler exposing <charconv> is needed to enable the std::to_chars/from_chars interop path
integration.platforms: x64, x86, arm, aarch64, wasm (emscripten), ppc64le, s390x tested in CI; bare-metal, RISC-V and LoongArch reported working via issues/PRs but not in the official CI matrix
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: covers the same numeric types as std::to_chars/from_chars, but c4::to_chars(substr, T) returns size_t and c4::from_chars(csubstr, T*) returns bool, unlike std's pointer-pair + to_chars_result/from_chars_result interface, so call sites must change

gotchas: Requires cloning with --recursive (or `git submodule update --init`) for the cmake/, fast_float, and debugbreak submodules; the amalgamation script is the alternative for header-only use

On MSVC, c4core deliberately disables std::from_chars in favor of fast_float ('prefer fast_float with MSVC'), so float from_chars comparisons on Windows are effectively fast_float vs. an MSVC STL that also uses similar techniques internally
A static-assertion failure in charconv.cpp on VS2019 was reported (issue #19, closed as duplicate in 2020) — worth checking current MSVC versions before relying on it
Float/double results in the README exist only as PNG charts (g++12.1 Linux / VS2019 Windows), not in the text MB/s table, which covers integers only
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick c4core's charconv when you already want its broader utility library (substr, span, error handling) and only need integer to/from-decimal speed; its documented integer wins (1.05x-2.44x over std) are smaller than Boost.Charconv's or rigtorp/CharConv's claimed multiples, so choose one of those instead — or fast_double_parser/fast_float — if isolated charconv or float-parsing performance alone is the goal.
verified_claims_summary: On Linux with g++11.2 Release, c4core's own CI microbenchmark (bm/bm_charconv.cpp) shows c4::to_chars beating std::to_chars by 1.07x-2.44x and c4::from_chars beating std::from_chars by 1.05x-1.54x across 8/16/32/64-bit signed and unsigned integers, measured in MB/s. Float/double comparisons exist only as PNG charts from a separate g++12.1 (Linux) / VS2019 (Windows) run; no CPU or hardware is disclosed for either run.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-03, ~149 stars); MIT-licensed core with permissively-licensed bundled dependencies (fast_float, sg14 BSL-1.0, debugbreak BSD-2-Clause), so it is safely copyable/vendorable, including via the single-header amalgamation script.
